$comment: Golden parser fixtures for DinnerDecider. Extracted verbatim from the Swift unit tests listed in each case's `source`. See shared/conformance/README.md for the runner contract. Do not edit a case to make a port pass; fix the port.

cases.description: Happy path: a single IdentifiedItem wrapped in a ```json code fence.
Model wraps the object in conversational prose on both sides. Both must be ignored.
cases.input: Sure! Here is what I found: {"name": "Large Eggs", "brand": null, "category": "dairy", "confidence": 0.8} Hope that helps.

cases.description: Explicit JSON null for the optional brand decodes to nil, not to the string "null".
Plain prose with no brace anywhere: extraction returns null.
cases.input: there is no json here at all

cases.description: TRUNCATED OUTPUT: an opening brace that never closes. Must return null, NOT a truncated prefix.
Balanced but illegal JSON: extraction SUCCEEDS because the scanner only balances braces.
Same input as object-unquoted-keys-extracts: extraction succeeds but the JSON decode fails, so decode returns null. The pair proves extraction and decoding are separate stages.
Valid JSON, but category and confidence are absent. Swift Codable requires both, so decode returns null.
EMPTY OUTPUT: the model returned nothing at all (what a stuck grammar sampler produces, and what AppModel substitutes when generateText throws). Must return null, never crash.
Braces inside a string literal must not affect depth counting.
Same input, decoded: the name keeps its literal braces.
Two top-level objects: only the first balanced one is returned, nesting handled, trailing content ignored (not an error).
CHANNEL-PREFIXED OUTPUT: everything up to and including the last <channel|> close marker is discarded.
cases.input:
<|channel>thought
The box says OATMEAL so name is Oatmeal.
<channel|>{"name": "Oatmeal"}

cases.description: No channel marker: the text is returned byte-identical.
CHANNEL-PREFIXED OUTPUT with a decoy: the reasoning contains {"name": "WRONG"}, which a naive first-brace scanner would return. Stripping the channel first discards it.
cases.input:
<|channel>thought
Let me build the JSON. Something like {"name": "WRONG"} but let me reconsider the category.
<channel|>{"name": "Oatmeal", "brand": null, "category": "pantry", "confidence": 0.95}

cases.description: Channel preamble AND a code fence around the answer. Proves the order of operations: strip reasoning first, then fences.
Happy path for the identify-all-items path: a one-element array inside a code fence.
Array preceded by prose.
Multi-item array spanning several lines; element order is preserved.
A top-level OBJECT where an array was expected is a hard miss: there is no fallback from the array path to the object path.
TRUNCATED OUTPUT: the array was cut off mid-stream. Must return null, not a one-element array.
CHANNEL-PREFIXED OUTPUT on the array path.
cases.input:
<|channel>thought
I see several items in this fridge photo.
<channel|>[{"name": "Yogurt", "brand": "Fage", "category": "dairy", "confidence": 0.91}]

cases.description: An empty array decodes to an EMPTY ARRAY, not null. "The model saw nothing" and "the model was unreadable" must stay distinguishable.
EMPTY OUTPUT on the array path returns null (no bracket found), which callers treat as zero items.
Happy path for the recipe bundle: the exact reply MockLLMService emits, deliberately wrapped in prose AND a code fence 'exactly like a real model tends to, so the parser is genuinely exercised'.
